findings.text: xfd_validate_state is the public validation entry that warns when xstate_op_valid deems a state and mask pair unusable. The restore flag distinguishes restore-like operations for init state handling.

xstate_op_valid compares per CPU xfd_state against stored xfd in fpstate. Equality allows use. Mismatch equal to current task stored value forbids use. Shared init_fpstate allows restore-like use only. Otherwise the routine discards disabled and already present components from mask and forbids use when anything remains.
xfd_update_static_branch runs at boot via arch_initcall and enables __fpu_state_size_dynamic when init_fpstate carries dynamic bits, otherwise keeps static sizing.
fpstate_free releases heap state with vfree only when the fpu object holds a separate allocation distinct from its embedded __fpstate, otherwise it does nothing.

validate_sigaltstack requires sighand siglock held by caller. It bases need on get_sigframe_size adjusted from fpu_user_cfg maximum to requested user size, then fails with shortage when any thread in the group has a smaller nonzero alternate stack.
get_sigframe_size returns max_frame_size for signal stack calculations.

__xstate_request_perm merges permitted with requested into a combined mask, derives kernel size with compacted layout and user size from user-supported subset without compacting, validates host alternate stacks, then publishes mask and sizes with ordered writes to guest_perm or perm.
xstate_prctl_req holds XFEATURE_MASK_XTILE_DATA at position XFEATURE_XTILE_DATA and zero elsewhere.

xstate_request_perm validates index against XFEATURE_MAX, looks up xstate_prctl_req with speculative guard, requires support in fpu_user_cfg maximum and fast accepts when xstate_get_group_perm already covers request. Otherwise it locks sighand siglock, rechecks, rejects locked guest permissions with busy error and otherwise expands via __xstate_request_perm.
xfd_enable_feature forwards fault information to __xfd_enable_feature with empty context. The restricted build variant of xstate_request_perm always denies with permission error.
xstate_get_guest_group_perm and xstate_get_host_group_perm expose guest and host group permission masks respectively.

fpu_xstate_prctl handles ARCH_GET_XCOMP_SUPP for support, ARCH_GET_XCOMP_PERM and ARCH_GET_XCOMP_GUEST_PERM for host and guest permission queries, and ARCH_REQ_XCOMP_PERM with ARCH_REQ_XCOMP_GUEST_PERM for host and guest acquisition restricted to 64 bit, rejecting others.

avx512_status skips PF_KTHREAD and PF_USER_WORKER tasks, otherwise reads avx512_timestamp with ordered load, converts elapsed jiffies to milliseconds with overflow capping, and emits a labeled decimal line showing negative sentinel when never used.
proc_pid_arch_status emits wide vector timing via avx512_status when X86_FEATURE_AVX512F is present and always reports success.
owner_name carries the value LINUX for core note ownership.

elf_coredump_extra_notes_write and elf_coredump_extra_notes_size return zero when fpu_user_cfg has no maximum features. Otherwise size accounts for note header plus aligned owner_name plus get_xsave_desc_size. Write emits header with NT_X86_XSAVE_LAYOUT type, owner, alignment, then dump_xsave_layout_desc records each carrying numeric type plus size plus offset with cleared flags via x86_xfeat_component, failing when emission or size verification fails.
elf_coredump_extra_notes_write and elf_coredump_extra_notes_size are the core dump integration points for extended layout notes.
xstate_copy_mode enumerates XSTATE_COPY_FP and XSTATE_COPY_FX plus XSTATE_COPY_XSAVE for selecting copy source format.
REX_SUFFIX is 64 on 64 bit and empty otherwise. XSAVE and XSAVEOPT plus XSAVEC and XSAVES with XRSTOR and XRSTORS denote respective save and restore operations with a memory operand.
FRED_DB_STACK_LEVEL equals 1, FRED_NMI_STACK_LEVEL and FRED_MC_STACK_LEVEL equal 2, FRED_DF_STACK_LEVEL equals 3. fred_rsp0 is a per CPU unsigned long holding entry stack pointer.

ftrace_arch_code_modify_prepare acquires text_mutex and sets ftrace_poke_late to defer patching. ftrace_arch_code_modify_post_process drains batches via smp_text_poke_batch_finish, clears the flag and releases the mutex.

ftrace_nop_replace supplies a five byte idle pattern from x86_nops. ftrace_call_replace resolves jump wrappers via ftrace_is_jmp with ftrace_jmp_get then emits JMP32_INSN_OPCODE or otherwise emits CALL_INSN_OPCODE toward the target.

ftrace_verify_code reads MCOUNT_INSN_SIZE bytes with copy_from_kernel_nofault and compares against expected old_code. Fault yields EFAULT and mismatch yields EINVAL with warning and stored ftrace_expected.

ftrace_modify_code_direct verifies then either queues via smp_text_poke_batch_add when ftrace_poke_late is set or patches immediately via text_poke_early. ftrace_make_nop allows direct idle conversion only from MCOUNT_ADDR and otherwise warns. ftrace_make_call converts idle to active for module load via direct path.
ftrace_modify_call always warns and returns EINVAL as unsupported.
ftrace_update_ftrace_func repatches ftrace_call and ftrace_regs_call to a new func using smp_text_poke_single.

ftrace_replace_code first checks every record with ftrace_test_record and ftrace_get_addr_curr against appropriate old pattern, aborting with ftrace_bug on mismatch. It then enqueues new patterns based on ftrace_get_addr_new or idle pattern, updates records and finishes the batch.
arch_ftrace_update_code forwards its command to ftrace_modify_all_code.
alloc_tramp allocates tracer trampoline memory via EXECMEM_FTRACE and tramp_free releases it.

OP_REF_SIZE is 7. ftrace_op_code_union overlays raw code bytes with a packed view of three opcode bytes plus 32 bit offset. RET_SIZE is five with CONFIG_MITIGATION_RETPOLINE else one plus CONFIG_MITIGATION_SLS selection.

create_trampoline clones ftrace_caller or ftrace_regs_caller templates based on FTRACE_OPS_FL_SAVE_REGS, appends x86_return_thunk jump or return sequence, clears direct call optimization for register variant, applies text_poke_apply_relocation, stores ops pointer, rewires op_ref reference, installs handler call under text_mutex, sets FTRACE_OPS_FL_ALLOC_TRAMP and hardens with set_memory_rox, freeing on failure.

set_ftrace_ops_ro write protects owned trampolines. calc_trampoline_call_offset derives call position from template choice. arch_ftrace_update_trampoline creates on first use, ignores foreign trampolines lacking ownership flag, otherwise updates destination with smp_text_poke_single under text_mutex.
addr_from_call reads CALL_INSN_SIZE bytes, requires CALL_INSN_OPCODE and computes destination from displacement, warning and returning null on fault or opcode mismatch.
pr_fmt prefixes tracer messages with module name.
